peerMapping.justification: The block reserves GOLD as the primary hedge and uses peers to span silver's two engines: monetary-metal flow and industrial demand. COPPER carries the largest peer weight because it is the closest industrial-metal expression of the same global manufacturing and electrification cycle, even though its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 6.262 USD millions is far below SILVER at 32.581 USD millions. SP500 and CL add the broad risk-on/risk-off channel and the energy-inflation and mining input-cost channel with displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 50.729 USD millions and 40.091 USD millions. SNDK, MU and TSLA are smaller end-demand proxies for electronics, memory, solar and electric-vehicle silver use; their displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 98.839 USD millions, 21.299 USD millions and 4.787 USD millions, but single-name earnings and idiosyncratic risk keep their weights below the macro and commodity legs. Weights are positive, sum to exactly 1, and favor economic comparability first while using displayed 24-hour perp liquidity in USD millions as a constraint rather than the sole ranking signal.

peers.name: Copper
peers.reason: Copper is the best industrial-metal peer because silver demand is tied to electronics, solar, electrical contacts and brazing, while silver supply is often a byproduct of copper and other base-metal mining; both react to global manufacturing, construction and electrification. Its 6.262 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is much thinner than SILVER at 32.581 USD millions, so the high economic comparability is tempered by a liquidity discount.

peers.name: S&P 500
peers.reason: The S&P 500 is a broad risk-on/risk-off and real-rate proxy: silver can trade like a growth-sensitive industrial input when equities rise on manufacturing optimism, and can be sold for liquidity in broad risk-off episodes. The 50.729 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is deep, but the equity beta is indirect versus a metal, so the weight is meaningful but not dominant.

peers.name: WTI crude oil
peers.reason: WTI crude adds the energy-inflation and mining input-cost channel: oil shocks move inflation expectations and real yields, and diesel and power costs affect mine supply. With 40.091 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity, it can carry a meaningful weight.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: Tesla is a small end-demand proxy for electrification and solar, where silver is used in vehicle electronics and photovoltaic cells; it is high beta and single-name, and its 4.787 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity is low, so the weight is kept minor.

primary_index_hedge.name: Gold
primary_index_hedge.reason: Gold is the cleanest primary hedge for silver because both are precious metals driven by real interest rates, the US dollar, inflation-hedging demand and safe-haven flows; it offsets the monetary-metal component when silver's industrial beta is not the main driver. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 23.982 USD millions, close enough to SILVER at 32.581 USD millions to be executable while still being a distinct metal.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
